sec: Goodpasture active management, treatment & transplant note · p782

items.q: All of the following are conditions requiring active management in pulmonary renal syndrome EXCEPT:
opts: Positive ANCA serology with fibrous crescents only
Ongoing pulmonary haemorrhage
Sr. creatinine <5.5 mg/dL with normal urine output
Type IV RPGN
items.exp: Conditions requiring active management: ongoing pulmonary haemorrhage; Sr. creatinine <5.5 mg/dL with normal urine output; new cellular (non-fibrous) crescent; and type IV RPGN. (Book p782)

items.q: The serum creatinine cut-off below which active management is indicated, provided urine output is normal, is:
opts: 5.5 mg/dL
2.5 mg/dL
8 mg/dL
10 mg/dL
items.exp: Condition 2 requiring active management: Sr. creatinine <5.5 mg/dL with normal urine output. (Book p782)

items.q: A new cellular crescent, as opposed to a fibrous crescent, is one of the conditions requiring active management.
opts: True
False — only fibrous crescents warrant active management
False — crescents are never an indication
True, but only in type V RPGN
items.exp: Condition 3: a new cellular crescent (non-fibrous) requires active management, since fibrous crescents represent old, irreversible scarring. (Book p782)

items.q: The treatment listed for Goodpasture disease/pulmonary renal syndrome is:
opts: Mainstay PLEX (plasma exchange therapy) plus steroid and cyclophosphamide for 3–6 months
Mainstay steroids alone at high dose, continued for 3–6 months, without exchange
Rituximab monotherapy for 2 weeks followed by lifelong azathioprine maintenance
Antibiotics with supportive dialysis alone until the antibody disappears from serum
items.exp: Treatment: mainstay PLEX (plasma exchange) + steroid and cyclophosphamide for 3–6 months. (Book p782)

items.q: The listed duration of steroid and cyclophosphamide treatment with plasma exchange is:
opts: 3–6 months
2 weeks
12–18 months
5 years
items.exp: Mainstay PLEX + steroid and cyclophosphamide for 3–6 months. (Book p782)

items.q: A patient with Goodpasture syndrome has completed treatment and is anti-GBM antibody negative. He asks about definitive treatment. The book's answer is:
opts: Renal transplant — after antibody negativity for 6 months
Renal transplant — immediately, since antibody status does not matter
Lifelong dialysis — transplantation is contraindicated
Renal transplant after 2 weeks of antibody negativity
items.exp: Definitive treatment: renal transplant, performed after the antibody has been negative for 6 months. (Book p782)

items.q: In Goodpasture syndrome there is no recurrence of the disease after renal transplantation.
opts: True — recurrence is not described after transplant
False — recurrence occurs in 50% of transplants
False — recurrence occurs in 5% of transplants
True, but only if plasma exchange is continued after transplant
items.exp: Note: in Goodpasture syndrome there is no recurrence after renal transplant — in contrast to Alport syndrome, where the α3 defect gives a 5% chance of post-transplant Goodpasture syndrome. (Book p782)

items.q: A 22-year-old man with Alport syndrome received a renal transplant 6 months ago and now has haematuria, a rising creatinine and positive anti-GBM antibody. Which statement matches the book's note?
opts: The α3 chain defect of Alport syndrome gives a 5% chance of post-transplant Goodpasture syndrome
This is expected recurrence of Alport syndrome in 50% of grafts
Anti-GBM disease cannot occur after transplantation
This indicates a de-novo membranous nephropathy
items.exp: Note: in Alport syndrome, due to the α3 (collagen) defect there is a 5% chance of Goodpasture syndrome after renal transplant — unlike Goodpasture syndrome itself, which does not recur post-transplant. (Book p782)

items.q: Fill up: In Alport syndrome, the post-transplant risk of Goodpasture syndrome is ______%.
items.exp: Alport syndrome carries a 5% chance of Goodpasture syndrome after renal transplant because of the α3 chain defect. (Book p782)
